evidence: paper: A_n = \mathcal{A}_n, \qquad B_n = u_{\theta,n}\,e_\theta, \qquad p_n = q^{-2A+\lambda_n}\,\Pi_n, \qquad T_n = q^{-A-1/2+\lambda_n}\,\mathcal{T}_n.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Three of the four entries match with the paper's exponents exactly: p_n with -2A + λ_n (basePressure), and the stress pair T = (T_θ, T_z) with -A - 1/2 + λ_n (baseStressTheta, baseStressAxial); A_n is streamFactor/summedPotential as in (5.27). The fourth differs in form: the Lean slow base has no separate entry B_n = u_{θ,n} e_θ. The azimuthal part is carried as the axial component K = swirlPotential (exponent 1/2 - A + λ_n on -C⁻¹∫_0^X φ_n) of the same vector potential, and is produced by the same curl; by velocity_zero/velocity_one the K-part of the curl is (-r ∂_s K) e_θ, an azimuthal field of the paper's shape, so the route differs but reaches an azimuthal field. The paper instead keeps B_n as a field and cuts it directly, relying on azimuthal fields with θ-independent amplitude being divergence-free (the Lean generic lemma, exists_realization, does provide that route through its B argument with hdivB/htan, but the slow base does not use it). Lean's divergence-freeness is then automatic, being a curl.
